(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, target_door_open) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, target_room_entered) -> u4

(u4, target_picked_up) -> u5
(u4, else) -> u4
(u5, else) -> u5
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, key_found, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, has_matching_key, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, target_door_open, u3) -> 0.1
(u3, target_room_entered, u4) -> 0.1
(u4, target_picked_up, u5) -> 1.0
feedback: The RM faithfully encodes the task as a strictly ordered chain. The state order u0..u5 matches the event order the environment forces: key_found cannot precede has_matching_key, target_door_open cannot precede has_matching_key, and target_room_entered/target_picked_up cannot precede target_door_open. The intermediate states for has_matching_key and target_room_entered are not over-specification: both events are forced between the named milestones (carrying the key is required to unlock; entering is required to reach the ball), so the accepted trace language is identical to the literal three-milestone task (find key, open locked door, then pick up the ball) while giving denser, still bounded progress shaping (0.1 x 4 + 1.0, max 1.4). Deadlock-free: in each state the only firable chain event is the awaited one (e.g., in u2 target_room_entered cannot fire before target_door_open; in u3 target_picked_up cannot fire before target_room_entered), so no completing trace gets stuck. Latch handling is correct: key_found and target_room_entered fire once and re-truths fall to else self-loops. Conditions that can turn false (has_matching_key, target_door_open) correctly need no regression edges, since the task is achievement-based and physics guarantees the key is in hand at the unlocking toggle; drop/re-pick and shut/re-open flows still progress (in u2 else holds until the door opens; a re-opened door re-firing target_door_open in u3/u4 is absorbed by else). Every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant events (turns, moves, unrelated toggles, repeated latch truths). Predicate-only events: all five labels are defined labeling-API propositions; no invented or color-hard-coded predicates, consistent with the mission-derived target/key color. Format: header present, STATES declared, INITIAL_STATE declared, nonempty FINAL_STATES (u5) that is declared and accepting, reached only via target_picked_up (mission completion), with (state, event) -> state and (state, event, state) -> reward rows in the paper's shape; terminal u5 is absorbing with no spurious reward. Minor optional polish only: intermediate weights could be renormalized so the total sums to 1.0; no changes required.

feedback: All five declared propositions are implemented and the function set is exactly the declared set — none missing, no undeclared extras. key_found matches the documented view reading (latch on env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] OR built-in any over env.gen_obs()['image'] with cell[0] == 5); it iterates the array without NumPy method calls, so it is sandbox-safe, and the None/empty guard on previous_valuation is safe at step 0. target_room_entered is the correct latch: previous valuation OR (ax >= width - S and the chained row-span check 0 <= ay - (S-1)*B <= S-1), doorway cell included. The three conditions read only current state and never touch previous_valuation, and no function mutates the environment or episode memory. The B computation (max ball y over the grid, default agent y, divided by room_size - 1) is exactly the documented formula, and the ball's row identifies the target room row. has_matching_key deviates stylistically from the notes' 'carrying.color == L' but is provably equivalent: the candidate accepts when the carried key's color equals some door on column width - room_size within the target room's row span; per the layout evidence (500/500 layouts) that wall span holds exactly one door — the locked target door — and other same-color doors on that column sit in other room rows, which the span filter excludes. So it reduces to carrying a key of the locked door's color. target_door_open likewise finds the door by place (column width - room_size plus row-span filter), not by is_locked, so it stays correct after unlocking clears is_locked, and it checks is_open only after None/type guards. target_picked_up compares env.mission to the concatenated 'pick up the <color> ball' string, matching the documented f-string form without assuming a fixed color. No imports, no actions, no side effects; all env attribute accesses (mission, agent_pos, carrying, grid.get, gen_obs, width, height, room_size, episode_memory) are within the documented Labeling API, grid lookups stay in bounds, and empty cells are guarded before attribute reads. Syntax is valid Python; chained comparisons, nested comprehensions, and max(..., default=...) all parse and evaluate correctly. Approved as aligned with the environment semantics and the reward machine's event order.
